tagline: Two-lane forest roads connect the Iron Range with Lake Superior
intro: The Superior National Forest Scenic Byway links the Iron Range and Lake Superior’s North Shore on paved, two-lane roads. Its scenery includes north woods, lakes, creeks and marshes, with hardwoods turning red and yellow among tall pines in fall. A State Scenic Byway since 1999, it offers the wooded journey and birdwatching opportunities highlighted by Explore Minnesota.

The designation first covered 61 miles from Aurora to Silver Bay. In 2014 the route grew westward to Gilbert, bringing its length to 78 miles. Along the corridor, taconite shaped two towns: Hoyt Lakes was created in 1955 to serve a mine, while Silver Bay was built to process ore arriving by train from Babbitt.

That longer route begins at State Highway 37 and Sparta Road, then passes through Biwabik before reaching Aurora. From Aurora, the drive continues to Hoyt Lakes, then arcs south on the stretch called Skibo Lookout Road. Skibo Vista overlooks the Laurentian Divide; farther east the route passes Fairbanks, Bassett and Toimi. Beyond Toimi, it follows County Road 15 to Lax Lake Road, turns south, then heads east into Silver Bay, ending at Highway 61 near the North Shore.

moments.title: Skibo Vista
moments.text: Skibo Vista looks across the Laurentian Divide, on the stretch south of Hoyt Lakes that takes its name from the overlook. During migration, hawks can be seen passing over the divide here.
moments.notice: Watch for migrating hawks over the Laurentian Divide.

moments.title: Toimi School
moments.text: Toimi’s schoolhouse grew from one classroom to two as its Finnish immigrant community outgrew the original school. Built in 1913, it closed in 1942 when students began traveling by bus to Two Harbors. Storage and garage use followed, before volunteers restored the building in the 1990s. They replaced the floor with wood from an old high school gymnasium and rebuilt a wall with matching siding. The front remained largely untouched, retaining two entrances, cloakrooms and the former teachers’ living quarters. The small pumphouse outside is a reconstruction, used to display photographs of the area’s history.

moments.title: Silver Bay
moments.text: Silver Bay began in 1954 as a company town built to process taconite arriving by train from Babbitt. The ore came from 60 miles northwest; Silver Bay itself has no taconite mining facilities. Black Beach carries another part of that industrial history in its taconite tailings. It opened to the public in 2015 after the city and state DNR negotiated beach access with the mining company. Black Beach Park contains three beaches and a municipally owned campground. The North Shore National Scenic Drive also runs through town, linking this forest journey with the Lake Superior shore.
